prompt:
Image 1 is a frame from our film and is the authority for the look of this old western town; a wooden water tower stands in its distance. Make one freestanding wooden water tower: a round plank tank bound with iron hoops and a shallow conical shingle roof, standing on four tall timber legs with diagonal cross bracing and a simple ladder up one leg.
Framing: one single image (not a collage, not a reference sheet) of only this structure, seen in a three-quarter front view from slightly above eye level, the whole structure in frame from its foundation to its roofline with clear margin on every side. It fills most of the frame.
Setting: it stands alone on a plain, seamless light-grey studio backdrop with a matching grey floor. No street, no dirt road, no sky, no hills, no other buildings, no people, no animals, no vehicles, no props other than those named above.
Light: soft, even, neutral studio light from the front, no harsh shadows, no sunset glow, no warm cast, no light coming from inside windows. Glass reads as dark, slightly reflective panes.
Materials are physical and real: weathered grey-brown planks with dark water stains, rust-red iron hoops, sun-split timber legs. Photographic realism, natural colour, full-bleed image filling the whole frame; no film border, no caption, no watermark, no text, no lettering, no logos; any sign board is blank wood. Not an illustration, not a painting, no HDR, no sharpening.
